holidays.name: National Lost Sock Memorial Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day of mourning for every sock that vanished between the washer and the dryer. Hold a moment of silence, then dig out that lonely orphan sock and give it a new life as a dust rag or a puppet.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance. Its origins are a bit murky, but it reportedly goes back to a promotional products company's creative director around 1999. It has since been adopted by laundry lovers everywhere.
holidays.funFact: Socks have an odd talent for disappearing. Mismatched socks are so common that some people now buy them on purpose, so no sock ever ends up officially lost.

holidays.name: National Butterscotch Brownie Day
holidays.description: A day for chewy, brown-sugar-and-vanilla bars with a caramel-like flavor. They're also known as blondies. Bake a batch, add some chocolate chips or nuts, and skip the cocoa.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. The treat itself dates back to the 19th century. Its recipes likely evolved from older baked goods such as medieval gingerbread-style cakes.
holidays.funFact: Butterscotch brownies get their flavor from brown sugar rather than cocoa. That makes them a blonde cousin of the chocolate brownie, and the reason they're nicknamed blondies.
